comments.author: Ilionikoi
comments.body_html:
they have no precedent for it realistically. the game boy is no longer sold, therefore game boy emulators do not infringe on their IP because they are not competing on a market, especially when gb emus are free.

this is different for games, as the IP being protected would be the entire franchise. distribution of old pokemon games for example is an infringement because it sets a precedent for a lawsuit on the basis of butting into the market for pokemon games, even without selling them, by providing a product even for free that might pull people away from buying one of nintendo’s newer pokemon entries. this is why rom distribution is something people might get in trouble for, but creating an emulator for an old console that isn’t in circulation anymore is fine; you would still need to dump your own games that you legally acquired manually, theoretically. supposedly.

allegedly.
